title: Proto-Mishkenaz 'Urgesten': grounding the gestural-origin claim in gesture-first language research
question: What does the current cognitive-science and linguistics literature establish about gestural origins of language - pantomime and emblematic gestures, the gesture-first hypothesis, home sign and emerging sign systems such as Nicaraguan Sign Language, and the cultural evolution of gesture-to-speech pathways - and which of those documented findings best serve as real-world anchors for presenting Proto-Mishkenaz as a system of Urgesten (proto-gestures)?
why_now: proto-mishkenaz.astro is one of the six pages named in the pending migration (EXT-ECO-MISH-20260714-001), whose content is defined in the migration task as Urgesten; that page will publicly present the language's origin layer, and grounding it in actual gesture-origin research determines whether the presentation is credible and educational rather than a bare assertion.
